title.narrative: Strengthening SIND Mental Health's International Volunteer Capacity

description.narrative: SIND’s volunteer-led unit, Sind Mental Health (SMH), partners with Global South organizations to advance rights and care for persons with psychosocial disabilities. Following internal transitions and onboarding two new volunteers, SMH aims to strengthen continuity and knowledge transfer within its partnership with the National Organization of Users and Survivors of Psychiatry in Rwanda (NOUSPR). This initiative combines a planned monitoring visit with structured capacity building. It supports new volunteers Daiana Micaela Kejwan (coordinating the Rwanda partnership) and Nikita Sepopo Dzegle (supporting implementation) in assuming expanded roles in SMH’s international engagement. The visit provides practical training in monitoring and collaboration with user-led organizations, backed by mentorship from experienced SMH volunteers and SIND staff. It strengthens the SMH–NOUSPR partnership through direct engagement, enhancing trust and mutual accountability. This cost-efficient approach embeds learning into active projects and aligns with Disability Fund guidelines.
